clue.text: If returning to beach divided by path, find the rods and reels

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the little word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: a word divided by another is split open with the second word sitting inside it

parts.note: a shingle beach is one of pebbles
a tack is the course a sailing boat steers

explanation.surface: An angler cuts across a path to the beach and finds rods and reels lying there.
explanation.walkthrough: A tack is a sailing term: the course a boat steers into the wind, here standing for a path. The path word is inserted near the end of the beach word, before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rods and reels are the main items of equipment an angler carries, the gear known collectively by this phrase.

clue.text: Arbitrate with Milan FC before Venezia lose their back three

indicators.note: losing the back three means the final three letters of the city name are dropped

parts.note: Inter Milan is one of the two big football clubs of Milan
taken as written, the Italian name of Venice

explanation.surface: A referee steps in when Inter Milan play Venezia, two Italian football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in between disputing parties and settle things is to mediate, close in sense to acting as arbiter.

clue.text: Being hirsute can be risky!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: informal for dangerous or frightening

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek warning that having lots of body hair is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shaggy or covered with hair, and in informal speech also means alarming or dangerous.

clue.text: Spicy seeds little Margaret's crackers about

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: crackers and nuts both mean crazy
Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Little Margaret's Christmas crackers are filled with spicy seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is' joining the pet name to what goes round it; crackers looks like the party novelty but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard aromatic seeds of an evergreen tree are grated as a spice, and each seed is called by this name.

clue.text: Used dignity in clearing up

indicators.note: something used has been worn and knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their self-respect while doing the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing up and putting things neatly in order are the same household activity, both gerunds.

clue.text: Winner laid a hundred on that French leading runner to take gold

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
que is French for that

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of runner
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A punter bets a hundred on a French favourite to win the gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who defeats others, a victor, so a winner in the broad sense.

clue.text: Big lager order

indicators.note: putting things in a new order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar asks for a big glass of lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something of considerable size, plain synonyms.

clue.text: Eight stone German dog just eating tangle weed

parts.note: Hund is German for dog

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside, so the jumbled letters go in the middle

parts.note: just and right both mean fair

indicators.note: a tangle is a jumbled mess, so the following word's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed up

explanation.surface: A heavy German dog is chewing on a tangle of weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: A British hundredweight is 112 pounds, and a stone is 14 pounds, so it is exactly eight stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In imperial measure this unit weighs 112 pounds, which is the same as eight units of fourteen pounds.

clue.text: It is said skinny Ms Minogue needs love and loud respect

indicators.note: something said is spoken out loud, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: Kylie Minogue is the Australian pop singer; skinny is thin
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
f, forte, is the musical mark for loud

explanation.surface: A slim Kylie Minogue craves affection and noisy admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high esteem is to admire them, the same as respecting them, both taking an object.

clue.text: Tinned tuna cooked without nitrogen is wholesome

indicators.note: cooked food is changed from its raw form, so the letters are reworked
without means lacking, so the chemical symbol is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Canned fish cooked without nitrogen preservatives makes a healthy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: One N comes out of TINNED TUNA before the remaining nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoilt and free of contamination is pure, and so healthy or morally sound.

clue.text: Direction found by old prime minister

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four compass points
second meaning: Lord ..., British prime minister during the American War of Independence

explanation.walkthrough: Lord North led the British government from 1770 to 1782.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cardinal compass point and is also the title of an eighteenth-century British premier.

clue.text: Classic hat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the five Classic English flat horse races
second meaning: the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are five big British horse races for three-year-olds; the one at Epsom gives its name to a hard round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epsom race is one of the Classics, and in America the same word is a bowler hat.

clue.text: Pleasure seeker of note, taking alternative pain cure

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous hedonist turns to alternative medicine for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean devotes themselves to the enjoyment of fine food and comfort, a hedonist.

clue.text: Look at the French car models with holes!

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
le is French for the
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so two of them are Ts

explanation.surface: Check out the French car models, full of holes!
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelets are small reinforced openings in fabric or leather for laces to pass through.

clue.text: Top manager could kill to incorporate beginnings of independent venture

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so these letters sit inside the verb

parts.note: to execute is to put to death

indicators.note: beginnings are the first parts, so only the opening letters of the next words are kept

parts.note: the first letters of independent and venture

explanation.surface: A furious boss could murder someone over an independent start-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior person in a company with authority to make decisions.

clue.text: Find point in tasteless decoration

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter sits within the adjective

parts.note: garish means vulgarly showy
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone spots the point of some tacky ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a small decorative addition to a dish of food, an embellishment.

clue.text: Find Ian in kindergarten, hiding writing material

indicators.note: the words are hiding something inside them, so look within the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across these words, dropping the first F and the end of the last word

explanation.surface: A teacher looks for little Ian, who is hiding in the nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense black ink is used for drawing and lettering, so it is something one writes with.

clue.text: At which point we hear: "Put on ''eadgear!"

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words count for their sound, here in a dropped-H accent

parts.note: to put on headgear is to wear a hat, said with the H dropped as the clue's spelling shows

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style command at some moment to put a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''eadgear tells you the speaker drops their aitches, so hat becomes 'at.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereat is an old-fashioned conjunction meaning upon which or at which moment.

clue.text: Boil in a suit in North Africa!

definitions.note: Tunisia is a country in North Africa, not the whole region

indicators.note: boiling sets things bubbling and churning, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wearing a suit in the North African heat, you would boil!
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'in' is part of the surface: the answer is a country located in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a Mediterranean country lying in the northern part of the African continent.

clue.text: I forged new metal support for fireplace

indicators.note: something made new is put into a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blacksmith boasts of forging a new iron stand for the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, or andiron, is one of a pair of iron stands holding logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Shows off by having fun round Los Angeles back street

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
LA is the standard abbreviation for Los Angeles

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction, right to left

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A show-off parades round the back streets of Los Angeles having a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display something ostentatiously, which is exactly showing it off.

clue.text: Viral infection found in fuel mixture engulfing New Zealand

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation
a mixture is a blend of jumbled ingredients, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the anagram needs these four letters plus an A that the clue never prints, the setter's slip
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: A virus has turned up in a contaminated fuel mixture from New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed supplies no letter for the final A of the answer, so the wordplay falls one letter short; the setter presumably meant 'a fuel mixture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is an illness caused by a virus attacking the respiratory system, so a viral infection.

clue.text: Confine dealer in stolen goods

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to enclose with a barrier
second meaning: slang for a receiver of stolen property

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the criminal noun are unrelated senses of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pen in with a barrier; as underworld slang it is a receiver who sells on loot.

clue.text: Stole sh-sharp tool

parts.note: the stammered start of the next word, taken as written
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A stammering confession that someone stole a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a past-tense verb, but it is the noun for a wrap worn over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf or wrap worn around the shoulders, just like a shawl.

clue.text: Freddie recklessly sat on top of Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: doing something recklessly means wildly and without order, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
RR is the badge and abbreviation of Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: Someone called Freddie carelessly perched on top of a Rolls-Royce car.
explanation.walkthrough: Freddie Starr was a British comedian and impressionist famous in the 1970s and 80s; in a down clue 'on top of' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the British comic points to his surname, which completes the familiar celebrity name.

clue.text: Far Eastern city is discovered with an oil well

indicators.note: something discovered has been found lurking, so look for it inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of with across an into the start of oil

explanation.surface: An Asian city strikes it rich when it finds an oil well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' just completes the oil-well picture; the answer sits inside 'with an oil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam, in South-East Asia, once called the Far East.

clue.text: Romanians move to a place in Italy

definitions.note: San Marino is an independent republic surrounded by Italy

indicators.note: when people move they are shifted about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of Romanians emigrate to a spot in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic enclosed entirely by Italian territory, so it lies geographically within Italy.

clue.text: Officer's three-wheeler causes total stoppage

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer, with the possessive S
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: An army officer's tricycle somehow brings everything to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: When workers in every industry down tools together, all work ceases nationwide in one mass walkout.
